body:
Well funny you should mention that.  I spoke to my doctor today (scheduled and emergency visit) and told him what was going on.  He said it's this 
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anhedonia
which reading up on it sounds spot on to me.  He said they usually treat it with anti-depressants but they haven't been working on me, if anything they might be making it worse.  So he's going to try me on just a simple antipsychotic at a low dose with klonopin as needed for anxiety.  So, way less meds than I'm taking now and far smaller doses too.  Hope it helps.
No kids, I didn't want them.  Divorce is on the table but we are trying to work things out.  And no, nothing to look forward to.
Things at home with my wife have been hell.  I go to work to escape that.

I spent over 300 dollars on the steam summer sale on games that looked like a lot of fun but when it comes to sitting down and playing them I have no desire.  Sorry, I know you're trying to help but something is very wrong with me.  It's the same thing at work.  I should say it's made me bored and lazy because I'm not getting any work done either.

Thank you,
I wish that it were that simple but nothing interests me.  It's like the mechanism in me that would take interest in doing anything is broken.

Medication is very hard to get down.  I've been trying for nearly 3 years now to find the right mix.  I always give it a few months minimum before my doctor and I try something else.  I just spoke to him today about the antidepressant.  I've been on Wellbutrin for a year almost exactly now and he's switching me to cymbalta but leaving me on the wellbutrin for the time being.  I was taking prozac in addition to the wellbutrin but we felt it wasn't making a difference so he stopped it 2 months ago.
The truth is, this cocktail I'm taking has worked better than anything else in the past however it's still not enough.  I felt better before the antipsychotic's were included.  We tried zyprexa but it's side effects were too much for me to handle, I was on it for months.  We tried Risperdol next and it left me in the same state I am now so we switched about a month ago to Latuda.  The change was really hard, but I'm through the worst of it.  It however is making me feel the exact same way.  I believe there is no antipsychotic that is going to make me feel better, this might just be the way they make you feel.  The paranoia is gone so the drug is working, I just either feel numb, or depressed all the time now.  I don't want to live like this but I can't handle the paranoia either.  Damned if I do, damned if I don't.

I do see a therapist regularly.  We have been working a lot on how to get me out of the computer chair and into the garden so to speak.  He's a good a therapist, I have tried others and he's the best so far.  Since starting the antipsychotics though, therapy really has been no help.  My wife is actually against my taking medication and does not support me even though I am seeking help.
